recognize_zh: 上下兩個視野中，箭頭所指的紅血球明顯比周圍大、呈飽滿的卵圓形且中央淡染區消失，這就是巨卵圓形紅血球（macro-ovalocyte）；背景還有許多卵圓形與少數淚滴狀紅血球，提示巨母紅血球性變化。
features: Scattered red cells distinctly larger than neighbors with a full oval shape (macro-ovalocytes, arrows)
Macro-ovalocytes are well hemoglobinized with little or no central pallor
Background anisopoikilocytosis with many oval/elliptical forms and occasional teardrop and irregular cells
No polychromasia, red cell inclusions or leukocytes in these fields; scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear (two fields) shows anisopoikilocytosis with numerous oval and elliptical red cells and occasional teardrop forms. Scattered macro-ovalocytes (arrows) are larger than surrounding red cells, fully hemoglobinized and lack central pallor. No polychromasia or red cell inclusions are seen. Findings are suggestive of megaloblastic change; macro-ovalocytes can be present even when the MCV is normal (e.g., coexisting iron deficiency or thalassemia trait), so B12 and folate levels should be checked.

ddx.vs: Non-megaloblastic macrocytes are round, often with target cells or polychromasia, whereas macro-ovalocytes are distinctly oval and fully hemoglobinized.
Elliptocytes are normocytic, more elongated with parallel sides and dominate the smear, rather than scattered enlarged oval cells.
MDS can show identical macro-ovalocytes but has normal B12/folate and dysplasia in neutrophils or cytopenias, requiring marrow evaluation.
